what: v6 (6 November 2026, decided with the user): drowning, a new version of waterline-reprise (v5's, kept as it was). v5's view f by day held 15 s while the proposed level is drawn rising to its height, months compressed into seconds: the water comes first where the visible ground is lowest, climbs past the plants, shortest first, and past the lens; then a hold from 2.25 m under. Storyboard material, not frames of the film.
said_so: SPECULATIVE AND DRAWN: the water, its rise, its ripples, reflections and murk, the lens crossing and the view from under the surface are drawn. Nothing here is observed, and nothing is generated by an AI tool: the plants are v3's procedural models, the scene the flight south's.

The level is a proposal: 12.7 m Baltic, the dead-volume level Vyshnevskyi & Shevchuk (2024, p. 286) propose for a refilled reservoir; 13.1 m in the scene's heights (EGM2008, Baltic +0.4 m, config crossing3d.bed baltic_m).
The bed's heights the water rises through are inferred (the waterline method, scene3d/bed.py; FABDEM shows the old reservoir as flat water), and the plants it climbs are modelled.

The time is compressed: the rise is drawn in 10 s. Reaching the level would take months (a rough estimate, not on screen and not a source: about 3 months for 11.4 km3 at the Dnipro's mean flow); no duration is shown.

The view from under the surface is a drawn convention: Snell's window is not drawn (from 2.25 m down a real eye looking 14 degrees up would see the surface as a mirror nearly everywhere but overhead), and the water is drawn clearer than the reservoir's was, so the tower and the lit wires can be seen.
The flow dashes are the film's drawing convention, at the record's state of 11 September 2026 (Ferosplavna-1 connected, Dniprovska cut). The far birds are v5's, drawn.
The sound is a montage from the soundscape's own material (drowning_sound.json); the line is synthesized and its muffling under water drawn.

camera.view: v5's (v3's view f): (4355, 6870) in the scene's metres, heading 22, pitch 14, 18 mm on 36 mm, still

level.source: Vyshnevskyi & Shevchuk 2024, p. 286 (reports/ZNPP speculative ending and ecology.md)
level.note: as v5.json: the datum (Baltic) assumed, not checked again here

water.how: a flat surface at height h(t), drawn per frame by composite_v6.py from passes rendered once (still_v6.py): from a still camera such a surface covers exactly the pixels whose visible surface lies below h, so the order between water and plants follows from the scene's own heights (pos2x.exr: one exact surface per pixel at 3840x2160; the picture drawn at 3840x2160 and reduced to 1920x1080, 4 samples a pixel at the water's edge)
water.start_why: just under the lowest ground the view shows (the lane's ground, 9.25 m at the camera; 0.2% of the pixels lie under 9.25 m). The channel and pools of the scene's own water are not in this frame.
water.ease: sin^2 ramps: speeding up over the first 20% of the rise, steady, slowing over the last 40%

look_from_above.source: the scene's own water material ('water': unlit body colour under a glossy reflection mixed by half its Fresnel)
look_from_above.reflection: traced in screen space at 960x540 through the picture's own surfaces (the reflected ray marched against the pass's distances; off the picture or missing: the overcast sky), blurred 0.8 px
look_from_above.shallow: the ground shows through the first 0.12 m of path in water
look_from_above.ripples_note: drawn: band-passed noise tiles drifting south-west with the current (roughly toward the camera), faded with distance

water.lens_crossing: the waterline sweeps up across the frame over 0.5 s as the level passes the eye (a drawn meniscus, as over a lens port)

from_below.how: under the surface: the scene's surfaces darkened with depth and absorbed along their distance into murk; above it: the picture above (static, line, moving wires, birds) displaced by the ripples' slopes, absorbed along the ray's path in the water, its brightness varied with the ripples; all drawn

water.plants: unchanged: v3's 56,053 modelled plants (v3/plants/plants_f.npz), none hidden or moved; they go under only because the level climbs past them

line.what: v5's blue line (still_v5.py contour, v5's render) held from the first frame, so the shot can follow the reprise; faded out as the water reaches it

label: PROPOSED LEVEL · 12.7 M · VYSHNEVSKYI & SHEVCHUK 2024 · REACHED OVER MONTHS · THE BED'S HEIGHTS INFERRED · DRAWN (white capitals, Helvetica Neue 16 px, a black box at half opacity, bottom left, the line's blue stroke before it as its key; throughout)
debris: not drawn (floating leaves and twigs were optional; left out)

render.engine: EEVEE (Blender 5.2.2) for the passes: the static picture 32 samples (v5's), the heights 1 sample with the pixel filter off; 3840x2160
render.from_v5: v5's moving pass frames 450-899 (the lit wires' flow and the far birds), its wires' matte and its contour pass, unchanged

frames.note: each frame drawn in numpy from the passes (no Blender per frame)

render.output: 1920x1080, 30 fps (a storyboard test; the final would be 60), 450 frames

sound.title: The drowning's sound (from the speculative soundscape's own material)
sound.from: Speculative crossing soundscape (mix.py): its synthesized line and three of its recordings, each cut, high-passed at 250 Hz, faded and levelled exactly as mix.py does, panned as there

line.name: Ferosplavna-1
line.made: synthesized by mix.py's line() (hum.py's 330 kV voice: 100 Hz and its harmonics, the 6th stressed, corona hiss and cracks), seed 330, the first 15 s of its 30 s, -30 dBFS RMS before the master
line.under: from the lens crossing (5.17 s) low-passed at 380 Hz and -6 dB, crossfaded over 0.3 s: a drawn convention for hearing from under the water
